text: Ha Tinh expands industrial land fund, creating room for large-scale projects
From 2026 to 2030, Ha Tinh province plans to establish and develop over 9,300 hectares of land within its economic zones and industrial parks.

This land fund is strategically allocated for industrial, logistics, commercial-service, energy, and urban development, aiming to prepare clean sites and create capacity to attract large-scale investment projects.

The Management Board of Ha Tinh Provincial Economic Zone recently issued Plan No. 186/KH-KKT, outlining the implementation plan for the Ha Tinh Provincial Land Fund Development Scheme for the 2026-2030 period across its economic zones and industrial parks.

The plan's core focus is to review, finalize legal procedures, organize the exploitation, and establish land funds with synchronized technical infrastructure to meet the demands for expanding production, business, and attracting investment.

According to the plan, for land within economic zones (excluding industrial parks), Ha Tinh will concentrate on reviewing, completing procedures, and developing a total area of approximately 4,573.94 hectares.
This includes 18 transitional projects from the previous phase and Q1/2026, covering 1,451.14 hectares.

An additional 2,565.5 hectares are projected for new development between 2026 and 2030, alongside resettlement land to facilitate site clearance for projects within the economic zones and industrial parks.

Notably, within the newly developed land structure, Ha Tinh has earmarked approximately 949.5 hectares for commercial-service, logistics, and seaport development; 1,313 hectares for non-agricultural production facilities and energy; and 303 hectares for mixed-use urban areas in Song Tri, Vung Ang, and Hai Ninh wards.
This structure reflects a strategic direction to expand development in areas with advantages in seaports, transportation, and regional connectivity.

Beyond providing space for industrial production, the locality also prioritizes the development of logistics services, urban areas, and energy, gradually forming an economic ecosystem linked to key economic zones.

For industrial park land, the plan sets objectives to focus on site clearance, completing land procedures, and attracting infrastructure investment for transitional, expanded, and newly planned industrial parks, totaling approximately 4,728.15 hectares.

In addition to completing site clearance for the remaining areas of Vinhomes Vung Ang Expanded Industrial Park and Gia Lach Expanded Industrial Park, Ha Tinh plans to implement 12 new industrial parks according to a defined roadmap.

During the 2026-2027 period, several industrial parks are slated for focused implementation, including Ky Trinh Industrial Park (387 ha), Ky Trinh - Ky Thinh Industrial Park (305 ha), Industrial Park at Lot CN16 (122 ha), Ha Vang Industrial Park (200 ha), and the Industrial Park west of the former Ha Tinh city, now in Toan Luu commune (198.6 ha).

Projects to be prepared and implemented in subsequent years include Nam Hong Linh Industrial Park (310 ha), Industrial Park in Viet Xuyen commune (170 ha), Industrial Park in Thach Xuan, Toan Luu, Ha Huy Tap communes (370 ha), and the concentrated Industrial Park in Vung Ang ward (622 ha).
Beyond industrial land development, Ha Tinh also aims to establish land funds for logistics projects, seaport services, energy, and supporting industries.
These sectors are crucial for enhancing production capacity, completing supply chains, and leveraging the advantages of the Vung Ang Economic Zone.

The identified projects include Son Duong Logistics and Post-Port Center (472.63 ha), Vung Ang Logistics Center (133 ha), North Central LNG Storage project (Vung Ang LNG Storage) (479 ha), Vung Ang III LNG Thermal Power Plant (67.67 ha), and a Stainless Steel Production Plant project (66 ha).
